items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: When I was in college I mean Freddie Hubbard was my idol. I loved Freddie Hubbard and I liked to play in that sort of way.

ctx.x: And the record companies seem to focus on a few of the “young lions” business and put their strength behind them.

Right, which is fine. I mean I don’t begrudge them. I mean I think most of the ones that get the attention are extremely talented and they’re terrific players. The only thing that bothers me a little bit is that it seems like some styles count today and others don’t, and if you look at it from a creative viewpoint it’s a little mysterious because to me it seems like if the young guy plays like Freddie Hubbard or Woody Shaw, that’s taken seriously. Whereas if you listen to Buck Clayton and Louis Armstrong that’s…
Jazz has moved awful fast in its history it seems like.
